📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that BATON ROUGE, Louisiana — Today, weeks after a national election revealed a country fed up with high prices and data centers, Louisiana residents and organizations rallied in downtown Baton Rouge against gas plants for a massive Meta data center. Marching and rallying with signs and megaphones, the group urged the Louisiana Public Service Commission (PSC) to reject Entergy’s proposal to build seven expensive, polluting gas plants for Meta’s Hyperion campus.

Recent findings suggest that entergy wants PSC approval to build seven additional gas plants for the Meta data center, which will need more energy than a city four times as large as Latest Orleans. The utility doesn’t want to implement the common-sense customer protections requested by numerous groups intervening in the case. Sierra Club has been urging rejection of this proposal for months because it presents a “substantial cost” that Entergy’s existing customers may be required to bear.

Due to Gov. Jeff Landry’s “lighting speed” initiative and a previous decision by a majority of PSC commissioners, the agency is rushing this proposal through and planning to provide only one opportunity for the public to speak out against this proposal: a December meeting when commissioners are scheduled to also vote on the proposal minutes later. Much of the analysis Entergy has submitted to the PSC has been shielded from public view by NDA restrictions.

In response to the PSC’s upcoming decision, Louisiana residents and Sierra Club staff, issued the following statements:.

Industry observers note that “It’s clear by now that Meta and Entergy don’t care much for normal Louisianans, but the PSC has a mandate to do just that. Instead they have denied  us a meaningful opportunity to speak on a project that will impact our state for generations,” mentioned Margie Vicknair-Pray, project coordinator for the Sierra Club and a Louisiana resident. “Commissioners must know that the people will not sacrifice Louisiana for one big, risky, expensive, polluting experiment. They must vote no on this outrageous corporate favor.”.

It has been revealed that “Any claims that Meta is fully paying its own way are false,” noted Darryl Malek-Wiley, a senior field representative for Sierra Club and a Louisiana resident. “These seven gas plants will guzzle our water, pollute our air, – and customers will be on the hook to pay if Meta walks away. We’re here to tell commissioners that we are done footing the bill for massive tech – especially considering the extreme lack of transparency surrounding this project.”.

In its testimony to the PSC urging rejection of Entergy’s proposal, Sierra Club called for:.

In negotiations, Entergy showed little willingness to consider or agree to any of these stipulations.

Separately, in Meta’s application to the LDEQ, it wants to modify its existing permit to add 44 fossil-fuel water boilers that will operate and emit pollutants around the clock. Because this would send total pollution for the permit beyond the minor-source permit limits, Meta noted that – instead of applying for a major source permit as required by the Clean Air Act – it simply wouldn’t count emissions from the previously approved 31 diesel generators when those are operating during emergency hours.

Sierra Club has urged LDEQ that it must consider emissions from those diesel generators running during emergency operations.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • From smarter waterproofing to 360-degree rail adjustment, Top Rack Technology is putting installer efficiency, rooftop flexibility, and cost control at the center of its latest product lineup.
  • As the solar industry continues to look for ways to reduce installation costs and streamline residential projects, mounting hardware is getting a fresh dose of innovation.
  • Its latest lineup reflects a practical approach to product development: addressing everyday installation challenges while keeping system performance, aesthetics, and affordability in focus.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From smarter waterproofing to 360-degree rail adjustment, Top Rack Technology is putting installer efficiency, rooftop flexibility, and cost control at the center of its latest product lineup.

As the solar industry continues to look for ways to reduce installation costs and streamline residential projects, mounting hardware is getting a fresh dose of innovation. Top Rack Technology, Inc. (TRT) is making that case at RE+ 2026, where the solar racking manufacturer is showcasing six new mounting solutions designed to simplify rooftop installations, improve flexibility, and help installers work more efficiently.

Its latest lineup reflects a practical approach to product development: addressing everyday installation challenges while keeping system performance, aesthetics, and affordability in focus.

Six Products, One Common Goal: Better Installation Efficiency.

Recent findings suggest that among the new offerings is TRT’s Full-Coverage Skirt System, which targets an crucial consideration in residential solar: appearance. By concealing exposed array edges, the system delivers a cleaner, more finished look that can help installations better complement residential properties.

Recent findings suggest that the fresh TRT-G2 Bracket takes aim at installation simplicity and competitive pricing. Designed around practical field requirements, the bracket can be paired with TRT’s ButyLok waterproofing component, creating an integrated attachment and roof-sealing solution.

Waterproofing is particularly key in rooftop solar, where roof penetrations are still a critical consideration for installers and property owners alike. ButyLok introduces a shoe-like component containing pre-applied, gel-like butyl material. When compressed by the G2 bracket, the material spreads across the intended sealing surface, potentially reducing manual sealant application and simplifying the installation process.

TRT is also introducing SAVRIX, another residential attachment option developed with manufacturing efficiency, installation practicality, and cost competitiveness top of mind.. Meanwhile, the RF-2 Rail Fastener is designed to simplify rail-to-bracket connections.

Recent findings suggest that top Rack Technology’s FreePivot Bracket features a 360-degree rotatable rail fastener and built-in height adjustment to accommodate varying rooftop conditions and simplify solar panel installations. Credit: Top Rack Technology.

It has been revealed that but perhaps the most versatile addition is the FreePivot Bracket. Its 360-degree rotatable rail fastener allows installers to accommodate attachment points that aren’t perfectly aligned. Built-in height adjustment helps compensate for uneven roof surfaces, while its all-metal construction supports durability. The one-orientation design and single-socket installation concept are also intended to reduce tool changes and keep crews moving.

Hardware Meets Digital Project Planning.

Beyond the six fresh products, TRT is showcasing its established portfolio, including the TRT 01 Rail-less Base System, TRT 02 Rail-Base System, and TRT 03 Tile Hook System.

It has been revealed that the organization is also highlighting its Online BOM Design Tool, which supports project setup, structural design inputs, module layouts, engineering verification, and automated bill-of-materials generation. Connecting digital planning with physical mounting solutions could offer installers and distributors a more streamlined path from project design to field execution.

Installation hardware doesn’t need to be flashy to make a difference. Improvements in attachment flexibility, waterproofing, assembly time, and aesthetics can translate into meaningful operational advantages.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

Biofuels in the EU Post-2030 Renewable Energy Framework

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (419 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A deep-dive exploring the impacts of potential EU biofuels policy scenarios.
  • The discussion around the future of the Renewable Energy Directive (REDIII) is underway as the European Commission devises what role renewable energy will play in transport in the post-2030 energy framework.
  • As the political priorities of the EU focus on energy independence and domestic industry, there is a renewed push for more first generation food and feed crop biofuels in the European transport energy mix.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A deep-dive exploring the impacts of potential EU biofuels policy scenarios.

The discussion around the future of the Renewable Energy Directive (REDIII) is underway as the European Commission devises what role renewable energy will play in transport in the post-2030 energy framework.

As the political priorities of the EU focus on energy independence and domestic industry, there is a renewed push for more first generation food and feed crop biofuels in the European transport energy mix. But these biofuels can have adverse impacts on the climate, environment and food supply chains.

To address these concerns, we have modelled three different policy scenarios to demonstrate the consequences of varying outcomes and their potential impact on the climate, environment and food security.

Our findings show that the current cap on first-generation biofuels set by the Renewable Energy Directive (RED III) can allow 72% more food- and feed-crop biofuels to be used in the EU transport energy mix, compared to what the bloc consumed in 2024.

When accounting for indirect land use change, even at current consumption, emissions from first generation biofuels already reach nearly 43 MtCO2e, about 23% more than the fossil fuels they replace.

When safeguards take the same form as stipulated in RED III and other key transport regulations, food- and feed-crop biofuel volumes, land-use area and emissions could all potentially double by 2040, emitting an equivalent to more than 5 million diesel cars.

In an unfavourable scenario, whereby the cap on first generation biofuels is harmonised at 7% across Member States’ transport sectors, volumes, land use and emissions would almost triple.

In a worst case scenario, where the cap on first generation biofuels is expanded beyond 7%, the negative consequences would be far heavier. We have used 10% as an example: volumes, land use and emissions could be four times today’s levels in 2040. Land dedicated to biofuels could reach 17.7 Mha, 18% of the EU arable land, an area larger than Greece, and emissions would exceed those of fossil fuels by 33 MtCO2e.

Industry observers note that for advanced and waste biofuels, which are limited in supply, we show that the road sector is currently overconsuming available feedstocks, which should be directed towards sectors that cannot be electrified, particularly aviation. Furthermore, recent cases of fraud have highlighted the risks of relying on third country exports, making the case that all palm oil derivatives should be phased out and that effective safeguards should be put in place to allow for the most sustainable feedstocks.

Smarter Cooling, Stronger Reliability: Advancing Wind Turbine Gearbox Performance

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, as the wind energy industry matures, operators and service providers are increasingly focused on maximizing turbine availability while controlling long-term maintenance costs.
  • Heat exchangers play a critical role in maintaining proper oil temperature and viscosity within wind turbine gearboxes.
  • “Wind operators today are balancing increasing performance expectations with the realities of aging fleets and rising maintenance costs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as the wind energy industry matures, operators and service providers are increasingly focused on maximizing turbine availability while controlling long-term maintenance costs. Although major drivetrain components often receive the spotlight, one overlooked system can have an outsized impact on turbine reliability and performance: gearbox oil cooling.

Heat exchangers play a critical role in maintaining proper oil temperature and viscosity within wind turbine gearboxes. When cooling systems become clogged with airborne debris, dust, or organic material, oil temperatures rise, lubrication performance declines, and component stress increases. Over time, these conditions can contribute to reduced gearbox efficiency, elevated maintenance demands, and avoidable downtime.

“Wind operators today are balancing increasing performance expectations with the realities of aging fleets and rising maintenance costs. Technologies that improve cooling efficiency and reduce service exposure can have a meaningful impact on long-term turbine reliability and operational profitability,” according to Mike Erickson, HYDAC’s Market Manager for the Wind Industry.

Traditional “panel cut” heat exchanger designs have long been susceptible to clogging due to their tightly packed fin structures. In many wind environments — particularly agricultural, dusty, or high-pollen regions — debris accumulation can severely restrict airflow. Oil leaks can further compound the issue by trapping contaminants within the exchanger core, making cleaning more difficult and labor intensive.

This operational challenge has driven the need for more resilient cooling technologies designed specifically for real-world wind farm conditions.

Recent findings suggest that HYDAC’s new “Square Wave” heat exchanger design represents a significant advancement in addressing these reliability concerns. Engineered to allow debris to pass more freely through the exchanger fins, the design minimizes clogging while improving cooling efficiency under demanding operating conditions.

Sources indicate that the importance of effective cooling cannot be overstated. Wind turbine gearbox oil typically operates within an optimal temperature range of approximately 45°C to 65°C. Even modest temperature increases can significantly impact oil viscosity. According to field data, a 12°C rise in oil temperature can reduce viscosity by nearly 28 percent — affecting lubrication quality and accelerating wear on critical drivetrain components.

It has been revealed that field trials have demonstrated measurable operational benefits from the Square Wave design. During a one-year trial on GE 1.x turbines, the upgraded exchanger consistently reduced clogging and lowered maintenance requirements compared to traditional panel cut cores. Operators reported reduced up-tower cleaning time and fewer temperature-related cooling faults.

Field validation across multiple turbine platforms has further reinforced the operational advantages of the Square Wave design. In one case study involving legacy 1 MW-class turbines operating in the Pacific Northwest, a major renewable energy operator installed pilot sets of Square Wave heat exchangers as part of a cooling performance evaluation. Installation teams reported the upgraded exchangers integrated seamlessly into the existing platform with no retrofit complications.

Sources indicate that after initial operating data demonstrated improved cooling consistency, the operator expanded the evaluation program with additional units. Long-term SCADA analysis later demonstrated turbines equipped with Square Wave technology operate approximately 20 to 25 percent cooler than comparable turbines using conventional heat exchanger designs under similar operating conditions. The data also highlighted another crucial advantage: the Square Wave cores continued to maintain airflow and cooling efficiency in debris-heavy environments where traditional exchanger designs became increasingly restricted over time.

The successful deployment also generated interest from additional wind service organizations seeking retrofit-ready cooling upgrades that could improve turbine reliability while reducing maintenance burdens across aging fleets.

“What operators are increasingly recognizing is that small improvements in thermal management can create meaningful gains in turbine reliability, maintenance efficiency, and long-term asset performance,” stated Erickson. “The field data we’re seeing continues to validate the value of designing cooling systems specifically for real-world wind operating environments.”.

More recently, long-term SCADA data from Mitsubishi platforms further validated the technology’s performance. After two years of operation, turbines equipped with Square Wave heat exchangers operated approximately 19 to 25 percent cooler than reference turbines using standard exchanger designs under comparable operating conditions.

For wind asset owners and service providers, the implications are substantial: Improved thermal management supports healthier oil viscosity, more stable gearbox operation, and potentially longer component life. At the same time, reduced cleaning frequency and fewer cooling-related service events translate directly into lower operational expenditures and increased turbine availability.

In a recent development, as the industry continues to prioritize lifecycle optimization and energy production efficiency, innovative subsystem upgrades such as advanced heat exchanger technology are becoming increasingly valuable. Rather than waiting for costly failures or performance degradation, operators are seeking practical retrofit solutions that improve reliability without requiring major system redesigns.

“Effective thermal management is critical to protecting gearbox health and maintaining oil performance over time. By addressing one of the most common causes of cooling degradation — debris accumulation — operators can improve uptime while reducing unnecessary maintenance interventions,” said HYDAC’s Erickson.

For wind stakeholders evaluating ways to improve gearbox reliability, reduce maintenance exposure, and enhance turbine performance, cooling system optimization deserves greater attention. Proven retrofit technologies like advanced heat exchanger designs can offer a practical path toward improved uptime and operational efficiency without requiring major system overhauls.

As fleets age and performance expectations continue to rise, collaboration between operators, service providers, and technology partners will be essential to building more resilient wind assets for the future. Now is the time to evaluate whether existing cooling systems are supporting — or limiting — long-term turbine reliability goals.

Recent findings suggest that “HYDAC’s goal is to help wind owners and service providers solve practical operational challenges in ways that create long-term value across the entire asset lifecycle. Innovations like the Square Wave heat exchanger are designed to improve reliability, simplify maintenance, and support greater energy production over time.”.

Don’t let cooling system limitations impact turbine performance.

Proactive cooling optimization can help operators reduce maintenance exposure, protect critical drivetrain components, and maximize energy production across the asset lifecycle. Oct. 17—AeviusClinical intelligence AI modelsSeries: N/AAmount: $22 millionInvestors: Led by Insight Partners.

Recent findings suggest that aevius is a newly launched Mass General Brigham spinout founded by veterans of AstreaZeneca-acquired Modella AI. The tech giant builds models that intake different forms of medical data to paint a multimodal picture of a patient's current state and trajectory. That information can then be used by healthcare, payer and life sciences organizations for potential application in care delivery, operational decision-making and clinical research.

Recent findings suggest that “Our mission is to make medicine computable,” Rowland Pettit, M.D., Ph.D., co-founder and CEO of Aevius, said. “As a physician-scientist, I’ve worked across many types of clinical data, and there is far more knowledge in those records than we’re able to use today. We’re bringing general medical intelligence to that data, so organizations can build on a deeper understanding for their patients.”.

Industry observers note that the manufacturer stated it prepares to use the $22 million launch money to support continued model and product development. It also plans to expand its engineering, clinical and commercial teams, as well as to focus on commercial deployment.

In a recent development, oct. 15—Abby CareFamily caregiver trainingSeries: CAmount: $82 millionInvestors: Led by Transformation Capital, along with CVS Health Ventures, Frist Cressey Ventures and Pivotal, with participation from existing investors Khosla Ventures, Thrive Capital and Sequoia Capital.

Abby Care is an AI-native home care startup that equips family caregivers with professional training, certification and ongoing support from dedicated RN care managers. The organization works with health plans to arrange care at home for families that need it. Abby Care's platform also gives care teams real-time visibility into care delivered in the home, helping ensure families receive the support they need while enabling health plans to verify that care is being provided. Fortune reported the series C round.

The U.S. faces a major healthcare workforce shortage along with a rapidly aging population, and waitlists of vulnerable children needing care, noted Havi Nguyen, founder of Abby Care in a LinkedIn post."Family caregivers already know their loved ones best and are in the home. They’re the first to notice when something isn’t right. At Abby, we equip family caregivers with training, AI, and support from our clinicians to deliver quality care. Our platform enables real-time capture of care data in the home. Health prepares and states deserve visibility and confidence that care is delivered as intended. Better care and program integrity go together," Nguyen wrote.

Abby Care functions as a Medicaid provider to pay caregivers within Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Massachusetts, Fresh Jersey, Pennsylvania and Tennessee.

So far, Abby Care has helped families deliver millions of hours of care across many states, the company's members had 40%+ fewer reported hospitalizations in year one, she wrote.

Today, the company serves thousands of families across eight states, with additional markets expected to launch soon, executives said.

The funding will enable the tech giant to bring its model to more families, deepen its work with health plans and continue building technology and clinical infrastructure, the company said in a blog post.

In a recent development, oct. 14—AllswellBehavioral health for LGBTQ+Series: Seed Amount: $7 millionInvestors: Rethink Impact, Magnify Ventures, Ulu Ventures and Hopelab Ventures, Techstars and Amboy Street Ventures.

According to recent reports, allswell offers one-on-one virtual therapy, group programs and trauma-informed care to LGBTQ+ patients. It is in-network with commercial and Medicaid payers. The startup, launched in 2025, intends to use the capital to expand beyond its DMV-area footprint, build out its clinical training program for therapists and launch psychiatric medication management next year.

Sources indicate that "Nobody realizes how significant this market is. Only 5% of Gen X identifies as LGBTQ+, compared with 25% of Gen Z. That's a massive generational and cultural shift, and we want to do for LGBTQ+ health what Midi did for menopause," Heidi Patel, managing partner at Rethink Impact, mentioned in a press release.

In a recent development, allswell's therapeutic models were built for patients navigating depression and anxiety, identity-specific trauma, family dynamics and social transition. It is also developing its own curriculum on PTSD and trauma care.

According to recent reports, the startup, though latest, is already seeing positive outcomes. The tech giant often keeps patients for over a year, rare for behavioral health. In its most recent cohorts, 77% highlighted improvements in anxiety and 71% showed improvements in depression after 60 days of treatment.

Recent findings suggest that "Our patients aren't used to being served with care and respect, or to having something built for them. ... This is a sleeping-giant category, and it has been underestimated at every step. Our ambition is to continue developing newly introduced, thoughtful clinical programs specifically for the LGBTQ+ community, regardless of the political climate," Dawn Androphy, co-founder and CEO of Allswell, said in an announcement.

Oct. 14—ReadilyArtificial intelligence compliance platformSeries: AAmount: $11 millionInvestors: Define Ventures led the funding round, with participation from Y Combinator and the California Health Care Foundation Innovation Fund.

It has been revealed that readily’s platform connects regulatory requirements with policies, assigned actions and supporting evidence to reduce manual research and review processes. When the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) releases latest rules, CEO and co-founder Edward Tiong said, the platform can analyze them against existing policies and contracts “in hours,” identifying gaps and action items for teams.

The tech giant’s work with healthcare organizations covers more than 25 million covered individuals across 46 states, according to its website. Tiong said revenue has grown 10x. Read the full story here.

According to recent reports, oct. 14—Probably GeneticAI platform powering the research, diagnosis and treatment of genetic diseasesSeries: AAmount: $12 millionInvestors: Round led by Threshold, with participation from Y Combinator and other existing investors.

The company’s primary product is a physician-ordered genetic test for undiagnosed rare disease patients, who typically face a seven-year diagnostic odyssey before getting answers. There are two pathways to testing: free testing, through pharma partnerships, and insurance-billed testing. The free programs address specific conditions, with a limited number of tests available at a time.

In a recent development, patients can check their eligibility by completing a health and diagnostic assessment online. Probably Genetic’s AI platform converts self-reported symptoms, medical records and biological data into phenotypic data that it hopes can be used to train AI models for precision medicine in the future. Thus far, it has collected data from 130,000 patients.

Probably Genetic stated the fresh funds would be used to grow the core part of the business, for hiring and to enter the drug discovery arena. Read the full story here.

Industry observers note that oct. 14—AllaraVirtual women’s health providerSeries: UndisclosedAmount: $30 millionInvestors: Led by Index Ventures and GV (Google Ventures), alongside new investors Camino Partners, Foreground and Family Fund.

According to recent reports, allara, founded in 2020, has expanded to serve a broader continuum of women’s health. The manufacturer aims to fill gaps in care for women often navigating an array of specialists. Each Allara patient is paired with a multidisciplinary team, including OB-GYNs, endocrinologists, registered dietitians and patient success leads.

It has been revealed that since its expansion nationwide last year, Allara has added urgent care visits for things like UTIs, bacterial vaginosis (BV) and STDs, and brought on more internal medicine providers to its interdisciplinary care team. It has also launched more supplements and medication delivery services.

Recent findings suggest that the latest funding will accelerate enterprise partnerships, expand Allara’s clinical infrastructure and support more AI features, executives said. Read the full story here.

Oct. 14—Confido HealthStartup building an agentic AI operating system Series: series A extensionAmount: $12.5 millionInvestors: Z47, formerly Matrix Partners India, led the extension round. Existing investors Together Fund and Blume Ventures also backed the series A extension.

Confido Health is expanding beyond AI voice agents to build out an agentic AI operating system that can execute administrative workflows across a medical practice.

The series A extension follows its $10 million series A round announced in September to continue scaling an AI platform for end-to-end healthcare operations.

Confido Health integrates with over 50 systems of record, including electronic health records, practice management systems, phone systems, billing systems and fax, without requiring any change to a practice's existing tech stack. Confido's AI agents can increase administrative staff's capacity to serve patients by automating routine tasks like appointment scheduling, insurance verification, billing and patient outreach, according to executives.

Confido Health executives assert that its agentic AI operations platform can actually execute administrative work across existing systems, helping practices increase capacity and control labor costs rather than simply giving staff another software tool.

Recent findings suggest that healthcare private equity veteran Justin Saks joined as an investor and board advisor. Read the full story here.

Oct. 13—SukiAmbient clinical intelligence Series: EAmount: $90 millionInvestors: Healthier Capital, Crosslink Capital and Hercules Capital. All existing institutional investors also backed the round, including Venrock, Flare Capital Partners, Hedosophia, Philips Ventures and Zoom Ventures.

Suki CEO and Founder Punit Soni told Fierce Healthcare the tech giant is investing in three areas with the fresh capital: advancing its AI, expanding its commercial organization and scaling its partner ecosystem.

The tech giant has raised more than $250 million to date, executives say. Patient encounters supported by its tools grew more than 190% year over year in 2026, with revenue doubling in 2025 and on track for similar growth this year.

Recent findings suggest that suki now works with over 250 healthcare organizations and more than 30 technology partners that embed its AI into their platforms, executives say. Read the full story here.

Sources indicate that oct. 8—OutroEvidence-informed medication tapering supportSeries: Pre-seed and seed Amount: $7 millionInvestors: Listen Ventures, Cake Ventures, Jason Calicanis’s LAUNCH, Actions Capital, Hannah Grey VC, SemperVirens, Brock Recovery Group, Pave Health Ventures, and more.

Outro aims to support safe deprescribing of medications, starting with antidepressants. The company combines specially-trained clinicians with evidence-informed tapering protocols, patient monitoring, psychosocial support and technology. Its program is available in 14 states.

"Deprescribing guidance has existed in countries like the U.K. for years," noted Mark Horowitz, M.D., Ph.D., Outro's co-founder, psychiatry researcher and deprescribing expert, in an announcement. "Yet in America, where antidepressant use is widespread, tapering support is very hard to come by, so millions of patients are left without support when they are ready to come off.".

The funding will support the growth of Outro’s deprescribing clinician network, further the application of AI to deprescribing-specific workflows, expand the organization’s tapering model into additional drug classes and grow existing partnerships with leading universities and advocacy groups.

Sources indicate that earlier this year, the Department of Health & Human Services announced a initiative to prevent the unnecessary initiation of psychiatric medications and support tapering and discontinuation for patients not experiencing clinical benefit. It recommended providers regularly review the risks and benefits of psychiatric medications and offer alternatives like therapy when clinically appropriate. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services also released guidance for providers on the importance of deprescribing.

Healthleap then pushes actionable risk scores into optimized electronic health record workflows to support clinicians in identifying, treating and improving their patients’ health.

Healthleap has initially focused on disease-related malnutrition, a condition that costs the U.S. healthcare system up to $58 billion annually. The company's platform connects healthcare recommendations to actual care, whether that means filling a prescription, ordering a lab test, scheduling a telehealth visit or booking an in-person appointment.

Oct. 6—VitalizeAI-powered operating system for staffing and schedulingSeries: AAmount: $31 millionInvestors: Oak HC/FT, Norwest Ventures, .406 Ventures, Constellation Ventures, Y Combinator and MemorialCare Innovation Fund.

Vitalize aims to supercharge health system capacity and operations with an artificial intelligence platform that unifies staffing, scheduling, flow and capacity.

At health systems, labor and capacity management are highly manual, inefficient processes that take up hours of administrative work each day.

It has been revealed that labor optimization is the key constraint behind patient flow, operational efficiency and financial performance across health systems, Veeraj Shah, co-founder and CEO of startup Vitalize, said. Capacity planning is the other half of the equation. Hospital revenue depends on matching patient demand to available beds and staff.

Vitalize founders view hospital staffing and capacity management as a complex logistics problem that directly affects finances, patient outcomes and clinician experience.

Vitalize positions its software as an "air traffic control" system for healthcare operations, helping health systems automate staffing, forecast demand, manage capacity and reduce reliance on overtime and agency labor, executives noted. Vitalize’s AI automates the most manual scheduling tasks for clinical leaders, while forecasting demand and orchestrating staff across thousands of beds in real time. The company's platform uses machine learning, optimization models and AI agents to forecast staffing needs, fill schedule gaps, automate staffing workflows and recommend patient placement decisions, Shah noted. Sources indicate that tiny was introduced in 2022, initially focusing on a microbiome test for babies and moms. Tiny expanded to a vaginal microbiome test, and today its adult tests have surpassed pediatric ones in volume.

The capital, which brings Tiny’s total raised to $46 million, will be used to advance research, expand provider education, scale the B2B platform and expand the patient-facing AI agent.

Artificial intelligence company EliseAI, which automates healthcare and housing systems, secured $350 million in financing Tuesday, reaching a $4 billion valuation.

Sept. 24—Basalt Health AI layer for post-acute care admissionsSeries: AAmount: $20 millionInvestors: NEA led the round, with participation from Frist Cressey Ventures and 25m Health.

Recent findings suggest that basalt Health uses AI to streamline post-acute care admissions. The manufacturer plans to use the capital to expand its platform and grow its team.

Sources indicate that basalt's technology automates the referral and admissions process for post-acute providers, analyzing incoming referrals from faxes, portals and EHR integrations and matching patients to appropriate facilities based on clinical and payer criteria. The company says its platform reduces administrative work and speeds placement decisions that are often delayed by manual processes.

According to recent reports, each year, roughly 14 million patients enter post-acute care—yet the placement process has failed to evolve. The archaic process typically involves case managers faxing lengthy clinical packets to 6.6 facilities per placement, then waiting for the right bed to respond. The resulting delays and mismatches contribute to an estimated $17 billion in avoidable readmission costs annually.

After nearly a decade at Accolade, where he saw administrative work increasingly pull clinicians away from patients, Ben Hackett founded Basalt in 2024 to build technology that fits existing workflows, reduces friction and gives care teams more time to focus on patients.

The startup reports strong early traction with major health systems. Basalt has been live with Lifepoint Health’s team since its seed round in 2025 and the company has reduced median chart processing time from 8.5 minutes to 1.2 minutes. Basalt is also being implemented across 49 additional Lifepoint markets by the end of 2026.

“Case managers are still sending 70-page packets and waiting for responses, while patients remain stranded in hospital beds,” Hackett, founder and CEO of Basalt Health, said. “Basalt turns that uncertainty into fast, defensible decisions. This funding gives us the power to transform one of healthcare’s most stubbornly inefficient systems.”.

Basalt looks to expand beyond admissions into discharge planning and payer workflows, positioning its AI platform as infrastructure for managing patient transitions into post-acute care.

If we can help employers get more from one of their largest and fastest-growing healthcare expenses, we make healthcare more affordable for companies and the people who work for them.".

It has been revealed that rightway will use the Series E financing to expand its AI capabilities and the technology that powers its pharmacy benefits model. "Our technology and AI pull costs out of a bloated ecosystem that has failed to be efficient and transparent. That combination of better economics, better technology, and human clinical expertise means better care for members and lower costs for employers.".

Gravity Rail released out of stealth with a platform that enables healthcare organizations and care teams to build and run their own AI-powered patient engagement workflows.

Co-founded by Dan Walmsley, chief technology officer, and Scott Hoch, CEO, Gravity Rail says it brings a fundamentally different approach to deploying AI in healthcare that shifts control from outsourced vendors and point solutions to the teams responsible for patient engagement and care coordination. Rather than offering a single AI agent or outsourced service, Gravity Rail provides a model-agnostic operating system for AI-powered engagement, where healthcare teams can build, certify, and run workflows using their own protocols—across phone, SMS, email, web, and messaging channels—without writing code or relying on implementation vendors.

The platform is designed for any healthcare organization or companies working with them—including health plans, provider organizations, contact centers, business processing organizations, digital health companies, and clinical trial platforms—that are responsible for managing patient and member engagement at scale.

Most AI tools are still deployed as isolated solutions that sit outside operational teams, but as workflows change, those systems rapidly fall out of sync.

In a recent development, "Payer rules change, protocols evolve, better models emerge, and updates require coordination with an external vendor. AI transformation has to happen inside the organization. We put control in the hands of the people doing the work, turning protocols into live infrastructure they can see, test, and evolve continuously. As models commoditize, the advantage shifts to the organizations that can adapt fastest," Hoch noted in a press release.

In current deployments, Gravity Rai says it has already demonstrated measurable impact. He subsequently led health AI at Hugging Face, the largest open-source AI platform, before founding Almanac Health.

Sources indicate that behavioral health providers operate on fragmented, legacy software technology stacks that were not designed for the complexity of today’s modern care delivery. Admissions teams juggle disconnected CRMs and intake tools, clinicians document in EHRs built off paper workflows, and billing teams rely on manual, error-prone workflows.

Ease was built from the ground up to replace this patchwork with one AI-native system purpose-built for behavioral health.

The manufacturer’s tech unifies customer relationship management, electronic health record and revenue cycle management into a single platform designed to materially improve access to care, clinician experience, and provider economics across the behavioral health ecosystem.

Ease designed its platform to span the full patient lifecycle, from referral and intake through clinical care, billing and collections. By consolidating what are traditionally six to 10 separate systems into one, Ease reduces administrative overhead, eliminates redundant workflows, and enables automation across the most cost-intensive areas of behavioral health operations, according to the company.

Sources indicate that ease already supports a wide range of behavioral health levels of care, including outpatient, intensive outpatient (IOP), partial hospitalization (PHP), residential treatment, detox, and inpatient psychiatry, as well as medication-assisted treatment (MAT) across applicable settings. Ease works with both independent providers and large, multi-location provider groups, serving organizations across the United States.

The company’s approach has already demonstrated meaningful impact for customers, including reductions in third-party software spend through consolidation, faster time-to-admission, improved clinical documentation efficiency and materially improved billing throughput and collections performance, executives said.

The latest funding will be used to expand Ease’s product and engineering teams, accelerate development of AI-powered automation across the platform and support continued growth with enterprise behavioral health providers.- Release.

Salma Health’s integrated model connects front-line clinical care with scientific research to deliver breakthrough therapies for individuals living with psychiatric and psychological conditions, memory and dementia disorders, headache and migraines and brain injuries.

The company operates specially equipped clinics for in-person healthcare services augmented by telehealth solutions. #6830. Almost 90% of Europe’s Battery Production at Risk from Franco-German Car Deal

📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

Almost 90% of Europe’s Battery Production at Risk from Franco-German Car Deal

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (434 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Europe has huge potential for battery plants but calls to weaken or delay the Industrial Accelerator Act and carmaker demands to weaken the EU’s CO2 standards, risk handing Europe’s battery value chain to foreign competitors.
  • It has been revealed that the Franco-German car deal will secure just 13% of Europe’s planned battery cell production in 2030, fresh T&E analysis shows.
  • Industry observers note that the IAA introduces local content requirements to ensure scarce public subsidies and corporate tax incentives anchor homegrown EU manufacturing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Europe has huge potential for battery plants but calls to weaken or delay the Industrial Accelerator Act and carmaker demands to weaken the EU’s CO2 standards, risk handing Europe’s battery value chain to foreign competitors.

It has been revealed that the Franco-German car deal will secure just 13% of Europe’s planned battery cell production in 2030, fresh T&E analysis shows. Weak Made-in-Europe rules, combined with weaker emission reduction targets, risks handing over the market for battery production to Europe’s competitors, states T&E.

Industry observers note that the IAA introduces local content requirements to ensure scarce public subsidies and corporate tax incentives anchor homegrown EU manufacturing. 100 GWh of cells and 250 GWh of cathodes could leak abroad because of weak Made-in-Europe rules, the analysis shows — equivalent to 1.5 million battery packs.

At the same time, Europe’s battery industry faces a double blow from the EU Parliament’s proposals to weaken emission reduction rules which will cut cell demand by 247 GWh or approximately 3.7 million EU made EVs between 2027 and 2032 — almost three times the annual capacity of Europe’s largest battery plant, LG Energy Solution in Poland.

Sources indicate that franziska Grüning, Raw Materials Officer at T&E, remarked: “The Franco-German deal is a disaster for Europe’s battery industry. Securing a full European battery value chain, from mining to production, and the high value jobs it will provide, should be a top priority for Europe’s leaders. Instead, they are debating how far to weaken rules that would secure domestically produced batteries. Weak local content incentives for batteries in the IAA will send a terrible political signal for the future of Europe’s battery industry. Homegrown companies struggling to cross the valley of death should benefit from an IAA demand boost.”.

Industry observers note that with many cell factories only just beginning to ramp up, most EU production expected by 2030 comes from plants that have not yet entered production. The future of factories such as Lyten (formerly Northvolt) in Sweden, PowerCo Salzgitter in Germany, or Verkor Dunkirk in France, could be jeopardised by this deal.

The EU’s battery industry must not go the same way as its solar panels industry, says T&E, which calls on the EU to reject the Franco-German deal proposal on batteries, and stick to the timelines and battery requirements of the EU Commission’s proposal. In addition, a strict Made-in-EU scope, or at most a narrow list of trusted partners of the EU27 plus the European Economic Area (EEA) and the UK, must be introduced, and there should be no further weakening of the car CO2 standards.

Chutes & Ladders—SimpliFed adds COO; Mayo Clinic names next CEO" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

According to recent reports, welcome to this week's Chutes & Ladders, our roundup of hirings, firings and retirings throughout the industry. Please submit the good news—or the bad—from your shop, and we will feature it here each week.

>SimpliFed, a virtual breast- and baby-feeding support platform, has welcomed Gemma Wenstrom as the manufacturer's latest chief operations officer. She will help create the systems, accountability and operational foundation required to support sustainable growth and strong outcomes.

Wenstrom hails from Kaia Health, where she was also COO, driving commercial delivery, newly introduced business development and product strategy.

Sources indicate that “SimpliFed has built an incredibly strong foundation centered around improving access, continuity, and support for families during pregnancy and postpartum,” noted Wenstrom. “I look forward to helping scale the operational infrastructure, systems, and team needed to deliver high-quality, patient-centered care while supporting the tech giant’s continued expansion and impact.”.

Sources indicate that earlier this year, SimpliFed also added Melissa Walsh, M.D., as medical director. Walsh is a board-certified OBGYN with nearly two decades of experience spanning clinical care, academic medicine, digital health innovation and maternal health equity. She was previously national medical director of OBGYN at Pomelo Care. At SimpliFed, she will lead clinical strategy and care model development.

Recent findings suggest that >Mayo Clinic has declared Matthew R. Callstrom, M.D., Ph.D., as its next president and CEO, taking over for Gianrico Farrugia, M.D., who in May announced plans to step down at the end of the year.

Sources indicate that callstrom, a radiologist, has been with Mayo Clinic since 2002 who is currently medical director for Mayo Clinic Strategy and its AI Program. He's also a member of its board of governors and board of trustees. He's credited for his role in the major nonprofit system's organizational strategy and integration of AI into care.

Farrugia, who has headed Mayo since 2019, plans to stay on through Dec. 31 to ensure a smooth handoff.

Sources indicate that >Carl S. Armato, president and CEO of Winston-Salem, North Carolina-based Novant Health, will retire at the end of this year after 15 years leading the system.

Armato joined the nonprofit in 1998 as vice president of finance and operations in its Charlotte and Winston-Salem physician divisions, and held increasing regional and organization-wide leadership roles over subsequent years.

He's credited with boosting access points and unifying Novant's "collection of strong regional organizations into a unified, innovative health system." He also headed substantial growth, with the organization today counting 45,000 employees, 22 hospitals and about 900 total locations.

In a recent development, with his retirement, current Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer John Gizdic will become president and interim CEO on Jan. 1, 2027. His resume includes over 30 years of healthcare leadership, including more than 20 with Novant.

> UnitedHealthcare has named Suha Assi as CEO of individual Medicare Advantage, per a LinkedIn post.

Assi previously spent nearly a decade as executive director for Medicare and Retirement in Tennessee, and she previously held roles based in the state for Cigna. She wrote in the post that the "relationships with our teams, providers and communities have shaped how I think about this business and, most importantly, the people we serve.".

"As I step into this national role, I’m excited about what’s ahead for Medicare Advantage," she wrote. "I look forward to working alongside teams and provider partners across the country to modernize how we work together, strengthen relationships, and find latest ways to deliver for our members.".

> Daryl Tol, president and CEO of General Catalyst's Health Assurance Transformation Tech giant (HATCo) is stepping down from the role, the venture capital firm's CEO Hemant Taneja shared Tuesday.

Tol had been with the firm for about four and a half years in the wake of his time as president and CEO of AdventHealth's Central Florida Division. During that time, he headed HATCo's partner and advisory network—helping grow it to nearly 40 providers, payers and other portfolio companies—and took the company's top spot partway through 2025. Of note, he helped HATCo close its acquisition of regional health system Summa Health and served as its interim CEO for much of the past year until the appointment of Jennifer Eslinger last month.

Tol is being succeeded by Reva Nohria, a founding member of the HATCo team who has been with General Catalyst since 2018. Taneja, in his announcement, noted her work at both organizations has encompassed investment, company creation and strategic partnership, and that she will continue as an investor at the venture capital firm alongside her newly introduced appointment.

Tol will support a smooth leadership transition and remain in an advisory role, a representative of General Catalyst told Fierce Healthcare.

According to recent reports, > Jennifer Shuford, M.D., is leaving her post as deputy director and chief medical officer of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Nov. 12, just four months after joining, according to a Washington Post report that was confirmed by the agency on Tuesday.

The agency told press in a statement that Shuford was departing "to spend more time with family." Her appointment was confirmed by President Donald Trump in April, and she joined in June.

Shuford is an infectious disease specialist who came to the federal stage from a role as commissioner of the Texas Department of State Health Services and before that, served as the state's chief epidemiologist. Notably, she was credited with heading Texas' response to a measles outbreak last year. Her departure comes as the CDC clashes with state health departments and other public health leaders over its response to a growing national measles outbreak.

Satish Pillai, M.D., is slated to fill the role in the interim as the agency seeks a replacement, the CDC said.

> Johns Hopkins Health System CEO Kevin Sowers is set to retire at the end of 2027.

Sources indicate that sowers has served as president and CEO of the Johns Hopkins system since 2018. He also previously spent more than 32 years as a leader within the Duke University Health System, including eight as CEO of Duke University Hospital.

Industry observers note that the early announcement of his retirement looks gives Johns Hopkins significant time to conduct a search for a successor, with Theodore DeWeese, dean of the medical faculty and CEO of Johns Hopkins Medicine, leading the charge. And I intend to keep that commitment," Sowers stated in a video message.

> Calley Means, a prominent senior advisor to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. closely aligned with the Make America Healthy Again Movement, resigned from his role on Thursday.

"More policy and cultural change has happened around these goals in the past two years than any time in history—and I know this movement is just getting started," he wrote.

According to recent reports, > The American Medical Association tapped Jennifer Goldsack as senior vice president and inaugural leader of the AMA Center for Digital Health and AI. "We are at a defining moment for medicine. Digital health and augmented intelligence are rapidly and fundamentally changing how and where care is delivered. For these tools to reach their full potential and be effective for patients, physicians must lead the way in developing and implementing them. Jennifer is the right leader for this moment because she knows how to bring physicians and innovators together and translate that collaboration into real-world impact on patient care," AMA CEO John Whyte, M.D., noted.

According to recent reports, “Reimagining how we care for people in the digital era has been the focus of my career, and we are at an extraordinary moment of opportunity,” Goldsack remarked in a statement. “We have powerful upcoming tools at our disposal and a responsibility to make sure we harness them to improve people’s lives. I’m thrilled to join the AMA and work alongside physicians and partners across healthcare. We’re going to set a high bar for what better healthcare looks like in the digital and AI era. And together, we will make it happen.”.
