📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sunshine State is facing an unusual bout of heavy rain and flooding in the middle of its dry season, which usually begins in November.

The unexpected weather has put pressure on drainage systems and left standing water in many communities, particularly those in South Florida’s Broward County and along Central Florida’s Atlantic Coast in places like Daytona Beach and Cape Canaveral.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 18, the western part of Broward County faced what meteorologists refer to as a “rain bomb.” In just 24 hours, West Hollywood received over 15 inches of rain, while surrounding neighborhoods saw about 10 inches.

Due to the severity of the situation, which has led to issues such as stranded cars and out-of-service traffic signals, Broward County and Hollywood declared states of emergency, with Hollywood officials encouraging residents to shelter in place and avoid unnecessary travel.

In a recent development, forecasters expect additional rainfall through the end of this week as well as 2 to 4 inches across Eastern Florida, with about 4 to 8 inches from Miami to Jacksonville between Tuesday and Friday. Some areas may even get hit with up to 12 inches.

It has been revealed that while the wet and windy conditions are expected to improve, the Southeast may see a cooler, rainier Thanksgiving this year. The rain could linger from the upper coast of Texas toward the southern Atlantic Coast throughout the holiday weekend.

Sources indicate that “The dry season doesn’t mean your house is in the clear. Florida is at the moment showing us that heavy rain can flood homes miles from the beach,” says John Espenschied, owner at InsuranceBrokers.com in O'Fallon, MO.

If you’re a Florida homeowner, these unexpected weather conditions are a reminder that flooding may occur year-round—even outside of the traditional summer, hurricane season.

They can also give you a nudge to review your home insurance policy as it relates to flooding and take precautionary steps to protect your property and loved ones.

Florida’s current flooding is drawing attention to the fact that many homeowners do not have enough insurance coverage to recover from the damage.

According to recent reports, the Realtor.com® 2026 Housing and Climate Risk Report highlights the financial consequences. It found that over 6% of U.S. homes face severe flood risk, representing almost $3.4 trillion in property value.

At the same time, the number of active flood insurance policies from the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) fell by 4.5% between May 2025 and May 2026, decreasing from 3.62 million to 3.45 million.

And the problem goes beyond coastal communities.

In a recent development, moody's U.S. flood risk analysis, which accounts for flooding from heavy rain and overflowing rivers rather than just coastal storms, found that potential uninsured residential flood losses could exceed $375 billion in a modeled 1-in-100-year flood scenario. This may result in a national insurance protection gap of 65%.

According to Chris Bacon, chief operating officer of Openly in Boston, there are four primary factors that explain why many homeowners are lacking adequate flood protection.

First, most homeowners do not live in the highest-risk flood zones, so they don’t consider it a significant peril. Second, the cost of flood insurance can be high, especially for homeowners in higher-risk flood zones.

“The additional cost can be a constraint of homeowners’ budgets, and thus they choose to not purchase the coverage,” explains Bacon.

Sources indicate that third, mortgage companies do not require flood coverage unless the home is located in a high flood risk zone, so homeowners simply skip it to save money. Finally, the coverage from the NFIP, which goes up to only $250,000, is often lower than what a consumer needs should there be a major loss.

While there are private flood providers that can cover higher limits, premiums can be significantly higher because pricing reflects each property’s individual flood risk.

According to recent reports, “That’s why working with an independent insurance agent is so critical. They can provide the right coverage advice and show multiple options so you can make an informed decision for your unique situation,” Bacon adds.

Sources indicate that if you own a home in Florida (or any other state where flooding may occur), take a close look at your home insurance coverage. Determine whether it covers water that rises from the street or yard. Unfortunately, most policies don’t.

In the event you don’t have flooding insurance, get quotes from both the NFIP and private insurers.

According to recent reports, “The federal program caps building coverage at $250,000. You can buy up to $100,000 in separate coverage for your belongings. If your home would cost $400,000 to rebuild, ask what it would cost to insure the extra $150,000,” adds Espenschied.

Don’t forget to compare deductibles and start dates, and remember that federal coverage usually takes 30 days to kick in.

John Dickson, president and CEO at Aon Edge, a private flood insurance provider based in Kalispell, MT, points out that deciding whether to purchase flood insurance is a question of values.

“When you get a picture of how much you can lose, choosing to purchase flood insurance becomes an easy decision,” Dickson explains.

Fortunately, there are a number of precautions you can take to reduce the risk of serious flood damage on your property.

“Keep gutters clear of debris, and remove or clear debris blocking nearby storm drains and install a sewer backflow check valve,” says Bacon.

If you have a basement, elevate HVAC equipment, electrical panels, and water heaters above expected flood levels where possible.

According to recent reports, outside of your home, grade soil away from the foundation and extend downspouts to improve drainage. Finally, keep sandbags or flood barriers on hand, and know your evacuation routes.

Industry observers note that if you have a swimming pool, proper pool preparation is key. Avoid draining the pool completely, as hydrostatic pressure from waterlogged soil can cause the pool shell to pop out of the ground.

“Instead, lower the water level slightly (no more than 1 to 2 feet) to allow room for heavy rainfall, turn off power to the pool equipment at the breaker, and secure or store loose pool furniture and equipment inside to prevent severe damage,” Bacon explains.

In a recent development, to protect personal property, particularly high-value, irreplaceable, and sentimental items, move them off ground-level floors and store them on upper levels or high shelves. Keep important documents, family heirlooms, and electronics in sealed, waterproof containers, and create digital backups of critical financial and personal records.

For furniture or heavier items that must remain on the ground level, use blocks or risers to elevate them above potential floodwater lines before severe weather arrives.

“None of these steps eliminates risk, but together they reduce damage and help lead to faster recovery,” adds Bacon.

#6791. 2027 Hyundai Elantra Feels Too Nice To Be Treated Like An Economy Car

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1219 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

2027 Hyundai Elantra Feels Too Nice To Be Treated Like An Economy Car

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1219 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, for the most part, economy cars are treated as fairly disposable pieces of equipment meant mostly for getting folks from Point A to Point B.
  • As with the redesigned Tucson, Hyundai put its entire back into its eighth-generation compact sedan, giving it a distinct and decidedly upmarket look, a premium-feeling interior, a cutting-edge brain with stellar interior tech, and a hybrid powertrain that'll get over 50 mpg, all while maintaining the idea that "affordability is standard," according to Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai's Senior VP of product planning and mobility strategy.
  • Full Disclosure: Hyundai paid for my food and transportation so I could check out the newly introduced Elantra and Tucson at a warehouse in Jersey City, New Jersey.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for the most part, economy cars are treated as fairly disposable pieces of equipment meant mostly for getting folks from Point A to Point B. They're not exactly treated with much care during their lives, and when they're used up, they're scuttled off to the nearest junkyard. More likely than not, that same fate will befall the 2027 Hyundai Elantra and 2028 Elantra Hybrid, and I don't think that's fair. Top to bottom and front to back, this little sedan is just far too nice to deserve a fate like that.

As with the redesigned Tucson, Hyundai put its entire back into its eighth-generation compact sedan, giving it a distinct and decidedly upmarket look, a premium-feeling interior, a cutting-edge brain with stellar interior tech, and a hybrid powertrain that'll get over 50 mpg, all while maintaining the idea that "affordability is standard," according to Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai's Senior VP of product planning and mobility strategy. While I haven't driven it yet, the slightly larger new Elantra seems mighty impressive when it comes to the design, feel and specs.

Full Disclosure: Hyundai paid for my food and transportation so I could check out the newly introduced Elantra and Tucson at a warehouse in Jersey City, New Jersey.

The first thing about the newly introduced Elantra that will jump out at you about is undoubtedly how it looks. It's the latest example of Hyundai's "Art of Steel" design language that we've previously seen on the China-only Ioniq V, Boulder concept and recently revealed Tucson. Hyundai also told me that the Elantra's design pulls from the N Vision 74 concept, and even though this is a totally different kind of car, you can certainly see those cues, especially in the wide fenders of the rear three-quarter section. The high-performance N version of the Elantra has already been spied, too, and it's going to look sick as hell.

The Elantra is slightly bigger than it used to be; 3.4 inches longer and 1.2 inches wider, to be exact, with 1.2 inches added to the wheelbase. Hyundai says the majority of that extra space goes to the second row, with gains in legroom (1.1 inches), headroom (0.7 inches) and shoulder room for rear-seat occupants, and now folks who accidentally had a kid will be able to better fit a rear-facing car seat.

In a recent development, despite the extra size and funky angles, the 2027 Elantra still cuts through the air with ease, achieving a 0.26 coefficient of drag. Apparently, H-shaped daytime running lights and taillights are very aerodynamic. Who knew? The wedgey front end, also reminiscent of the N Vision 74, doesn't hurt either, and neither do the flush-mounted door handles.

It all helps explain why the Elantra is a real fuel economy winner whether you're looking at the entry-level gas motor or the optional hybrid. Fitted with 16-inch wheels, the 147-horsepower 2.0-liter inline-4, with the help of a CVT, will return up to 35 mpg combined, according to Hyundai. The 155-hp hybrid's 1.6-liter four-cylinder is mated to a six-speed dual-clutch transmission and 1.49-kWh battery, and Hyundai states it's going to achieve up to 53 mpg combined, which puts it firmly in "really, really good" territory. There's no word on other performance metrics right now, but I wouldn't expect anything too exciting, if I'm honest. The hybrid also comes with a Stay mode that lets you run accessories off the hybrid battery rather than the ICE motor when stationary for longer periods of time.

While the exterior is full of hard edges and sudden cuts, the interior is a far softer, more inviting place, one that wouldn't look out of position on a car that costs far more than the Elantra's at the moment unannounced price would suggest. Hyundai calls the furniture-inspired design ethos "Curve of Upholstery," and it's supposed to be all about comfort, simplicity, and minimizing driver distractions. It not only looks pretty thanks to interesting styling and materials choices, but it also feels nice to the touch with solid build quality.

Recent findings suggest that hyundai notes Elantra is a "software-defined vehicle," which is pretty uncommon for an internal-combustion-powered car. Mostly Hyundai's spokespeople talk about its Pleos Connect operating system and its capabilities, like next-gen navigation (and AI assistance crap), and it explains why the interior's focal point is the 12.9-inch infotainment touchscreen in the center of the dash. The left section of the screen serves as a driver display showing speed and other pieces of vehicle information, while the rest of it is a regular infotainment screen with configurable widgets for media, maps, and everything else you can imagine — including things you can't imagine, since Pleos allows owners to download apps created by others.

Beneath the center screen are dual wireless 15-watt Qi 2.0 chargers and 100-watt ultra-fast USB-C charging ports for your many crucial devices, and you can run audio from mentioned devices into an optional 12-speaker Bang & Olufsen audio system. Not too shabby.

Then, behind the steering wheel is a slim 9.9-inch display that is meant to keep the driver's field of vision uncluttered and only display critical information like speed, as well as radio, map directions or a few other things via widgets. We first saw both of these screens in the Tucson, and they make the Elantra feel far more tech-forward than a usual compact sedan would. Adding to that tech-forwardness is Hyundai's SmartSense suite of driver-assistance systems, which includes the classics like lane-keeping assist, lane centering, adaptive cruise control, forward collision avoidance and blind-spot monitoring.

Sources indicate that at launch, the gas-only Elantra will come in SE, SEL Sport, and Limited flavors. As you may imagine, features and materials get nicer as you move up the range, but the 12.9-inch screen, adaptive cruise control, push-button start and a few other niceties are all standard from the get-go. Coming a bit later (no word on how much later) will be the 2028 Elantra Hybrid, which will come in SE Blue, SEL Sport, and Limited trims. It's the same deal as the gas car, but there's even more as standard, including dual-zone climate control and Stay mode.

Sources indicate that I know that right now the Elantra is shiny and new, with its covers just pulled off at the 2026 LA Auto Show, and soon it'll face the sorts of abuse that all budget-friendly cars do. Before that happens, enjoy the Elantra and what it has to offer the world, because it's not very often an automaker swings for the fences on a cheap vehicle like this. Yes, vehicles like the Corolla, Civic and Mazda3 are very solid, but they're never exactly inspiring — certainly not from a design perspective, at least.

Sources indicate that the eighth-generation Elantra elevates the segment, and it might force other automakers to rethink their budget vehicles as well. It certainly looks polarizing from the outside, and it won't be for everyone, but it's also distinctive, and that's something that is very hard to come by on a budget. If you're the type of person who appreciates that, plus a comfortable interior and tech that punches well above its weight class, then it's best you start getting ready now, because the Elantra is set to hit U.S. dealers in early 2027.

As more people recognize the value of owning older cars that are easier and more affordable to repair, options like this thoughtfully updated '68 Camaro SS get more appealing on a regular basis. Even if car repair costs are rising at an alarming rate, it's still worth looking at simple old cars. This particular 1968 Chevrolet Camaro SS is currently listed for auction on Cars and Bids, and it is powered by a 350 small block (possibly a 383 stroker engine — the seller isn't quite sure), with shifting done via a four-speed manual transmission. It has an Odometer Brand Discrepancy on its Massachusetts title, though, with unknown true mileage, which could end up making it an affordable, daily-drivable example of this classic muscle car.

It has smart upgrades like electronic fuel injection, an electronic distributor, four-wheel power disc brakes, power steering, and traction bars that should all serve to make it a friendlier car to drive on a daily basis, and an aftermarket head unit and speakers to make it friendlier to live with. It's got too much character to be winning any concours any time soon, so whoever ends up winning the auction might as well enjoy driving it.

Okay, so the odometer right now displays 6,300 miles, but it was replaced at some point, so that only indicates mileage put on after the odometer was replaced. That said, the ad says the current seller purchased it in 2025 and has added about 1,200 miles since then, which bodes well for its drivability. This is not a perfect car, with flaws including a sagging headliner, an inoperable parking brake, missing rear window cranks, holes in the glove compartment, and a disconnected fuel gauge, but it would make a great project for a dedicated gearhead.

From the photos, its exterior looks serviceable, with its share of little imperfections, but overall it looks pretty clean for a 58-year-old car. There's a bit of rust on the Cragar wheels, but nothing too serious. Unfortunately, it does have aftermarket LED headlights, which I'm not the biggest fan of, but it doesn't look as bad as it could. In the video included in the ad, the Camaro starts right up and idles smoothly without any puffs of smoke or any other immediately concerning symptoms — another good sign. I think I'd be willing to overlook its flaws if the price is right. What about you?

He wants to upgrade to something that gives him the feel of a sports car but still has room for the kids and is comfortable in traffic. With a budget up to $80,000, what car should he buy?

(Welcome back to What Car Should You Buy? Where we give real people real advice about buying cars. Do you want us to help you find a car? Submit your story on our form.).

I'm a nearing middle-aged dad who has been stuck driving his wife's hand-me-down Prius for the past few years. It gets me where I need to be, but there is zero joy in driving it. I had a VW GLI prior that at least felt like a car and not a golf-cart, but that got traded in for the family hauler. The trade-off is supposed to be that I can finally get a "nice car" for the big 4-0. While my initial aspirations were for a Porsche 911 (and always will be, maybe next decade), the reality of a daily commute and still needing to cart around the kids is a limiting factor. I am a surgeon- so occasionally there is a need for me to get to the hospital "quickly".

I want something fun to drive aggressively but can still be a comfortable daily driver for a slow commute.I want to feel the turns on the windy roads, when I can actually drive them. I am looking for something unique, and maybe efficient. I love the idea of a wagon or a sport-back. Something that will feel like a sports car even though I need to wait for a second mid-life crisis to actually get one. I do live in New England so, AWD would be preferred. I don't like Teslas but I would be open to an electric. Budget is up to $80,000.

Wants: AWD, sporty, comfortable.

While a Prius is a fine commuter car, you didn't spend all that time in Med school to take a stressful job and be bored while you drive. A 911 is the typical doctor's choice, but with the need for family hauling, the icon isn't going to work yet, plus the market for those cars is a bit bonkers so that $80,000 budget won't get you as far.

Sources indicate that since a door door won't give you the practicality you need, may I suggest what the Germans call a "Gran Coupe," which is essentially just a swoopy four-door with a hatchback. But the BMW M850 Gran Coupe will check a lot of boxes for you. It's comfortable in traffic, has plenty of room for the kiddos but also provides a turbocharged V8 with 523 horsepower paired with BMW's xDrive for all-weather traction. Here is a very nice Certified example not far from you in an excellent color combo for under $60,000.

Recent findings suggest that you're in a classic position here, Jesse: You want a 911, but your kids don't want to sit in those purely decorative back seats. I get it. I was that kid once, back in the third grade, when my dad got a 996 911 Cabrio with truly the worst back seats I've ever used. Luckily for you, though, Porsche itself has come up with the solution you need: The Taycan.

Two usable rows? Check. All-wheel-drive? Check. Wagon? Check. You're interested in non-Tesla EVs? Well, here's a fantastic one, and even available near you in a fantastic color. Your budget allows for it, your needs fit its bill, and there's no better car on Earth for you right now than a Taycan.

It has been revealed that this particular Taycan is available just over the border in Upcoming Hampshire, but it's not the only one near you. Find a spec and color you like, and get the electric Porsche that this point in your life demands. I vote this one for its beautiful blue shade, but you can be boring and get one of the gray ones in Massachusetts instead. I'll only judge you a little.

Get there in speed and style, without spending too much on fuel. I can't imagine anything more appropriate for an eco-conscious and budget-conscious surgeon than a long-wheelbase German executive sedan with big turbocharged V8 power under the hood, with a smidge of all-electric range to make your visits to the fuel pump less frequent.

Sources indicate that I found this nice black long-wheelbase 2018 Porsche Panamera Turbo S E-Hybrid "Executive" model on eBay for way less than your $80,000 budget, with a buy-it-now button pegged at $68,985. It's an older second-generation model, so the all-electric range is a little on the low end at just 14 miles, but depending on your commute, that could add up to quite the fuel savings, especially if you can re-charge at the hospital. And it'll look right at home parked next to the plastic surgeon's Mercedes.

They're hard to find, and the price premium might push them outside your range, but if you don't prefer the luxurious long-wheelbase, you might be able to track down a Panamera Turbo S E-Hybrid Sport Turismo wagon if you're patient. Good luck, doc!

Earlier this year, Optum Rx teased the rollout of latest pharmacy tools designed to address medication cost and access.

Now, the company is offering a look at how those tools work.

The pharmacy benefit manager remarked Tuesday that the tools build on Optum's fresh and more transparent pharmacy model, which the company announced in May and shifts to a fee-based structure. The model moves away from more traditional approaches linked to manufacturer pricing and prescription volume and offers clients a clearly defined fee structure.

In a recent development, the first platform, called Shop MyScript, allows members to compare prices for their medications as well as their options for pharmacies or delivery before the prescription is dispensed. The tool will notify members of potential cost savings shortly after a script is written.

It has been revealed that in addition, Shop MyScript embeds in the prescribing workflow, Optum noted, so that the member does not have to make comparisons after the fact. If they choose to keep the existing prescription, it will then be sent to the pharmacy.

Optum mentioned that early adopters have averaged $28 in savings through the program.

"People should have clear information about their medication costs and options when they can actually use it, not after a decision has already been made," remarked Katte Carey, president of Optum Rx, in the announcement. "These tools give people more information earlier in their journey, so they can make choices that work for them and get the support they need along the way.".

In addition, the pharmacy benefit manager announced Optum Assistant, a conversational AI guide that helps members complete routine tasks and track down key information. The tool can triage concerns on a range of topics, from questions about medication and benefits to pharmacy experience challenges.

If the AI guide can't address the individual's needs, they can choose to be connected to live support to find a solution. Optum said about 80% of conversations using the tool led to a resolution without needing a live advocate.

The final new launch aims to support cash-pay options, according to the announcement.

In a recent development, optum Price Wise will offer members a complete cost breakdown, including the price of a drug and any fees. That total, all-in price allows members to fully understand what their options may be and make the choice that works best for them at the pharmacy counter.

Recent findings suggest that the PBM stated new tools like these build on Optum's new and more transparent pharmacy model, which the firm announced in May and shifts to a fee-based structure. The model moves away from more traditional approaches linked to manufacturer pricing and prescription volume and offers clients a clearly defined fee structure.

It has been revealed that the Volkswagen ID Buzz has not been a massive hit in the US (where it’s just too expensive and doesn’t even provide a lot of range), but it’s still one of my favorite vehicles. I would certainly have one in my driveway if I had enough money for one. Part of what makes the ID Buzz so appealing is how it reminds one of the VW Hippie Bus of yesteryear, but that vehicle was super low cost as well as versatile and useful. The ID Buzz is sort of a deceiving imitation of that model, as it’s quite expensive (especially in the US) and doesn’t really provide a lot of extra utility compared to what’s on the market today.

However, the manufacturer has just rolled out a new version of the ID Buzz that is designed to allow for easy sleeping within the van. The “camper” version of the ID Buzz has a few special features for this. Also, just to reiterate, it’s not cheap. So it’s more a little luxury camper van for people with money than a way to get around and live freely for young people scraping by and vagabonds. The ID Buzz Beach, as it’s called, will start at around £54,000 in the UK. (Whether it will come to the US and at what price, who knows?) It includes the following:.

Interestingly, you can get this camper version of the van in either the 5-seat or 7-seat version of the ID Buzz.

Is this going to attract a lot of buyers? Almost definitely no. Is it super cool, though? I think so.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that remote control trucks are cool and all, but haven't you ever wanted to remote control something bigger?
  • Volvo's newly introduced tech, Remote Steer, is just that — a way to steer and control the firm's new VNX heavy-duty truck from a gaming style control from outside the vehicle.
  • In a recent development, it wouldn't be Volvo Trucks if safety wasn't first and foremost in mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that remote control trucks are cool and all, but haven't you ever wanted to remote control something bigger? Realer? Well, Volvo Trucks has your number. The firm just introduced a new feature that allows operators to remote-control their own heavy-duty vocational truck — so long as it is on a job site, that is, and going under five miles per hour.

Volvo's newly introduced tech, Remote Steer, is just that — a way to steer and control the firm's new VNX heavy-duty truck from a gaming style control from outside the vehicle. It may sound like a party trick, but Volvo actually makes a good case for its use: Rather than relying on communication between a driver and a spotter for precision jobs, like aligning a trailer hitch or pouring concrete, Remote Steer allows one person to do both jobs. A worker can stand behind their truck, at the trailer hitch, and use the remote to back the truck up perfectly without any risk of anyone saying "No, no, my left.".

In a recent development, it wouldn't be Volvo Trucks if safety wasn't first and foremost in mind. The operator is responsible for switching on the system in the cab and linking the cab to a VIN-specific remote control. The remote control is married to only one VIN number, so there can't be an switch-em-up which could result in everything from hilarious shenanigans to untimely death. There is also a very limited range on the controller, as well as emergency stop buttons on both truck and controller. You'll also need to have all the latest and greatest Volvo Trucks tech to make it work, like Volvo Dynamic Steering, I-Shift transmission, electronic braking system, and a Body Builder Module. If you have that stuff, you can get the module installed aftermarket at any time.

Will this truck replace workers on the job site? Probably not. Ideally, Remote Steer will be used on job sites as a way to help existing workers rather than as a way to replace them. If that's the use case the tech sees, it'll likely be a genuine boon to the folks who have to do precision maneuvers on their trucks all day long. Then again, you might not see it at all, as Volvo Trucks, while sold worldwide to the tune of 120,000 trucks last year, has a smaller footprint here in the U.S than competitors like Mack (which is now a part of Volvo Trucks) or Kenworth trucks.

Either way, we hope we get invited to this press drive. Five miles an hour sounds like peanuts and, on the road, it is, but you don't need much more to dig around in a life-size sandbox with your buddies. Volvo's next move should be expanding to front loaders, excavators and Volvo Trucks-branded microbreweries that allow you to dig around and drink an IPA at the same time. The money would print itself.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, dengane Omari Jack lived at 1321 Flatbush Ave., which collapsed last Wednesday, tragically killing eight people and wounding 18 more.
  • Recent findings suggest that "He was one of the lucky ones," a friend wrote on a GoFundMe campaign to support Jack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first of what is likely to be several lawsuits was filed in Kings County Superior Court on Monday, alleging widespread negligence by a host of landlords, construction companies, and contractors in last week's deadly Brooklyn building collapse.

In a recent development, dengane Omari Jack lived at 1321 Flatbush Ave., which collapsed last Wednesday, tragically killing eight people and wounding 18 more. Jack was at work at the time of the collapse, but he rushed home to see if his extensive reggae vinyl record collection, valued at $100,000, might be salvaged. It was a total loss.

Recent findings suggest that "He was one of the lucky ones," a friend wrote on a GoFundMe campaign to support Jack. "But surviving came at an unimaginable cost: in a matter of seconds, he lost his home, everything he owned, and a lifetime's worth of memories and work.".

Industry observers note that now, Jack is suing his landlord and management manufacturer, as well as a half-dozen companies affiliated with 2625 Bedford Ave., the lot adjacent to his Flatbush building. None of those entities has filed a response to the complaint yet in court.

It has been revealed that the suit alleges the building's owner, Isolag Realty Group, and the property manager, Olufemi Falade, failed to take action after he pointed out cracks in the facade of 1321 Flatbush Ave. earlier this year.

According to the lawsuit: “During October 2026, Plaintiff observed cracks at or near the Building's entrance, photographed those cracks, and reported the condition to the landlord or management responsible for the Building.”.

The suit goes on to allege that Falade “personally received or responded to the report of the cracks on behalf of the Building's ownership or management. Plaintiff was falsely told, in substance, that the condition was not the landlord's fault or could not be fixed.”.

Falade has appeared on the city's "Worst Landlord" watch list, put out by the city's Public Advocate office, six times in the past decade.

Jack’s suit also names several entities tied to 2625 Bedford Ave., the adjacent lot where excavation work was taking place at the time of the building collapse.

Those defendants include general contractor Townhouse Builders, d/b/a Promont; Latest Jersey–based LMW Engineering Group and its president, Jieming Wang; W6 Facility X, an LLC affiliated with Robert Fischman; and LLCs affiliated with lot owners Faigy Fischman and Judy Swimer.

The suit points to a pre-construction survey commissioned by the builders, which documented that the facade of 1321 Flatbush Ave. was in "poor" condition prior to the excavation.

"The Defendants, who were responsible for excavation, design, supervision, inspections and monitoring received, or in the exercise of reasonable care, should have obtained and considered, the Pre-Construction Survey to evaluate all relevant Pre-Construction Site Conditions and, in particular, the Building's condition and its need for support and protection before proceeding with work at the Construction Site," the suit alleges.

Furthermore, the suit notes the defendants "had actual notice through the surveys, reports, observations or complaints applicable to their respective work, or constructive notice because the conditions were discoverable through the inspections and monitoring they were required to perform.".

The suit also claims that "the excavation, inadequate structural protection, negligent engineering orinspection services, and failure to address the Building's developing dangerous conditionproximately and/or substantially caused the Building to collapse, causing Plaintiff's losses.".

Recent findings suggest that the 2625 Bedford Ave. construction project had a history of safety violations noted by the Department of Buildings. The demolition of a building that had previously been on the site was halted in March of this year after demolition contractor N Tech Design of America had failed to take proper safety precautions, including installing netting and putting up sidewalk shields, records show.

A month later, inspectors returned to the site and found that the demolition had gone ahead anyway, in defiance of the stop-work order, according to city records. A $10,000 fine was issued.

Industry observers note that in May, a city inspector issued additional citations and another stop-work order against the contractors for allegedly failing to ensure adequate protections of neighboring buildings and for deviating from approved construction plans. Within a week, the city lifted that stop-work order.

Jack is suing for compensatory damages, rent relief, and punitive and exemplary damages.

In an interview with Gothamist, he valued his lost record collection at more than $100,000.

“ Nobody has contacted me from the city for, like, ‘We found some stuff that is still usable.’ I didn't hear anything like that,” Jack told the outlet. “And I don't know who to reach out to either.”.

Thankfully, he'd been transferring many of his vinyl treasures into digital files prior to the collapse and had his hard drive with him at work when the building fell.

“ Every single day I was just backing up stuff. I don't know if it's intuition was telling me to do this. But I was doing it every day for the past week,” he added.

The GoFundMe to support Jack, who DJs under the name Roots Outernational, has raised more than $12,000 so far.

Recent findings suggest that last week, hours after the collapse, Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez opened a criminal inquiry into the collapse. No charges have been filed yet.

In a statement late Wednesday, DOB Commissioner Ahmed Tigani stated that the department was working with law enforcement in the ongoing investigation.

"The Department of Buildings is doing everything we can to understand exactly how this collapse occurred, so that the responsible parties can be held to account," said Tigani.

Tigani also revealed that neighboring 1323 Flatbush Ave., which was heavily damaged in the collapse, was unsalvageable and would have to be brought down in a controlled demolition.

Realtor.com® has reached out to Townhouse Builders, LMW Engineering, Jack, and Jack's lawfirm, Antin, Ehrlich & Epstein LLP, for comment. Isolag Realty Group and Falade were not immediately reachable for comment.

Common supplement could help fight psoriasis, scientists discover

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A widely available nutritional supplement derived from vitamin B5 may offer a promising latest approach to treating psoriasis, according to research from China.
  • According to recent reports, the findings, published October 27 in the Journal of Experimental Medicine (JEM), reveal an unexpected connection between cholesterol production and the immune system.
  • How Overactive Immune Cells Contribute to Psoriasis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A widely available nutritional supplement derived from vitamin B5 may offer a promising latest approach to treating psoriasis, according to research from China. Scientists found that pantethine can calm immune cells involved in autoimmune inflammation, preventing psoriasis from developing in mice and improving symptoms in a small human clinical trial.

According to recent reports, the findings, published October 27 in the Journal of Experimental Medicine (JEM), reveal an unexpected connection between cholesterol production and the immune system. By interfering with this process, pantethine may help reduce the excessive immune activity responsible for psoriasis and potentially other autoimmune diseases.

How Overactive Immune Cells Contribute to Psoriasis.

At the center of the discovery are dendritic cells, specialized immune cells that help organize the body's defenses. These cells act as coordinators, identifying potential threats and directing other immune cells to respond.

Industry observers note that dendritic cells perform this role by capturing foreign substances called antigens and presenting them to T cells, which are immune cells that recognize specific threats. They also release chemical signals that recruit additional immune cells and trigger inflammation.

Although these activities are essential for fighting infections, problems can arise when dendritic cells become excessively active. Instead of helping protect the body, they can contribute to persistent inflammation and autoimmune diseases such as psoriasis.

According to recent reports, "Emerging evidence highlights that metabolic pathways and their associated metabolites play vital roles in regulating immune cell function and autoimmune progression," says Wei-Na Zhang, a researcher at the State Key Laboratory of Biomedical Analysis in Beijing. "But therapeutic strategies targeting metabolism in inflammatory diseases remain underexplored.".

Zhang led the research alongside Qing Xia, Ai-Ling Li, and Tao Zhou, also from the State Key Laboratory of Biomedical Analysis, and Cheng-Xin Li from The First Medical Center of Chinese PLA General Hospital in Beijing.

Scientists Discover a Hidden Link Between Cholesterol and Psoriasis.

The researchers identified unusually high levels of enzymes called Vanins in dendritic cells from people with psoriasis and several other autoimmune diseases. These enzymes help regulate the processing of certain substances involved in cellular metabolism.

According to recent reports, when the scientists reduced Vanin levels, dendritic cells became less active and were less capable of stimulating T cells. They also found that a drug designed to inhibit Vanins prevented psoriasis from developing in mice.

Further investigation revealed why these enzymes might play such an important role.

In a recent development, vanins convert pantethine into vitamin B5, an essential nutrient that cells need to produce energy. Pantethine is already sold as a nutritional supplement and is commonly used to help lower blood cholesterol because it can reduce cholesterol production.

In a recent development, this connection is particularly interesting because cholesterol does more than circulate in the bloodstream. It also influences how immune cells function. Previous research has shown that cholesterol can stimulate dendritic cell activity, while elevated blood cholesterol is a major risk factor for developing psoriasis.

The team discovered that excessive Vanin activity reduces the amount of pantethine available inside dendritic cells. As pantethine levels fall, cholesterol production increases, causing these immune cells to become unusually active.

Restoring pantethine levels interrupted this process. The supplement reduced cholesterol accumulation within dendritic cells and helped suppress the excessive immune activation associated with inflammation.

"We found that pantethine administration effectively alleviated psoriasis in mice, suggesting that insufficient pantethine levels may be the crucial contributor to hyperactivation of dendritic cells and autoimmune inflammation following the up-regulation of Vanins," Zhang says.

Common Supplement Indicates Promise in Human Psoriasis Trial.

Encouraged by the laboratory and animal findings, the researchers investigated whether pantethine might also benefit people living with psoriasis.

In a recent development, they conducted a small clinical trial involving 24 patients with the condition. All participants received a topical ointment containing calcipotriene/betamethasone, a combination treatment used to control psoriasis symptoms. Calcipotriene is a vitamin D derivative that helps regulate skin cell growth, while betamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation.

Half of the participants also took pantethine tablets, allowing researchers to examine whether adding the supplement improved the results of standard treatment.

After 12 weeks, the patients who received pantethine alongside their prescribed ointment showed greater improvement in psoriasis symptoms. The benefits were especially noticeable among participants who had high blood cholesterol levels before treatment.

These findings suggest that pantethine could potentially serve as an additional treatment for psoriasis, particularly in patients whose cholesterol metabolism may be contributing to inflammation.

However, the trial included only 24 people, and the researchers emphasize that larger studies are necessary to confirm the supplement's effectiveness. The human results also do not establish that the same biological mechanism observed in laboratory experiments is responsible for the improvement in patients.

Sources indicate that "Our investigator-initiated clinical trial demonstrated encouraging therapeutic efficacy of pantethine as an adjunctive therapy in psoriasis, but these findings should be interpreted as proof-of-concept for clinical feasibility rather than direct mechanistic validation," Zhang states. "Overall, our study uncovers the Vanin-pantethine-cholestrol axis as a key metabolic pathway governing dendritic cell activation and provides a foundation for therapeutic strategies targeting several dendritic cell-mediated autoimmune diseases.".

Of course, most of us in the US and even in Europe know nothing or next to nothing about Leapmotor, but it has clearly been more effective than hundreds or even thousands of other companies that have tried to launch and scale up EV production.

One interesting thing to note regarding this milestone: it’s peanuts compared to Leapmotor’s plans for the next few years. In 2026 alone, Leapmotor plans to produce one million vehicles, and it’s on track to do so. That means that, this year, the organization plans to produce as many vehicles as half of Leapmotor’s cumulative total at the moment. So, it will just be sometime in the middle of next year that the company will reach 3 million cumulative EVs produced.

The company is now producing more than 100,000 vehicles a month — for four months running.

Recent findings suggest that naturally, the firm’s proposal is to keep growing. As part of that effort, it just rolled out a new model, the Lafa 5 compact hatchback, with pre-sales starting earlier today. Also, another new model, the D19 SUV, just had its 50,000th unit produced.

So, yes, keep an eye on Leapmotor. It’s already a wildly successful young EV firm, and it looks like it is going to continue growing fast.

Sources indicate that the nostalgic Eclipse is located in the middle of Vespucci Island, which is just off of Vice City. As you head toward Vice Beach, the home will be on your left. The massive wing of the real Mitsu is silver and black, while the animated rendition is green and black. Even the graphics, although the same colors, are splashed on slightly differently. The wheels are six-spoked, brushed-aluminum in GTA 6, while the film car featured seven spokes and was bright silver. Furthermore, the game vehicle feels a lot faster than what you'd get from O'Conner's decidedly non-turbo, naturally-aspirated 2.0-liter.

According to recent reports, but it doesn't matter. GTA 6 is a vivid representation of real life without using actual names of places and things, so yup, this is Paul's car ... I mean, Brian's. Whatever. Find it and furiously drive it through the streets of Vice City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Medicare Shared Savings Program saved $2.5B last year: CMS" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

The Medicare Shared Savings Program has reached the highest savings number in its history, according to new federal data.

In a recent development, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services said Tuesday that the program generated more than $2.5 billion in net savings for Medicare in 2025, making for the ninth year in a row that it led to cost savings. The agency added that every accountable care organization met or exceeded quality reporting requirements.

ACOs participating in MSSP earned $4.9 billion in shared savings payments during 2025, CMS said, with 80% of organizations earning performance payments.

As of 2026, 511 ACOs representing more than 700,000 providers are participating in the Medicare Shared Savings Program, which represents 12.6 million people enrolled in traditional Medicare, another record.

"Patients want doctors who work together, care that puts their needs first, and fewer unnecessary hurdles—that is what accountable care is designed to deliver," mentioned CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz, M.D., in the announcement. "These record savings show the power of rewarding providers for quality and coordination. We want more people with Medicare, and more of the providers who care for them, to benefit from this approach.".

Industry observers note that CMS stated that it wants to make it easier for providers to participate in MSSP if they choose, especially given the program's results to date. It included changes in the latest Physician Fee Schedule to encourage participation, including increased opportunity for certain ACOs to earn shared savings and new financial incentives to draw in first-time participants.

According to recent reports, in addition, CMS said that would create more predictable spending targets that make planning and participation straightforward. The agency is also aiming to streamline patient notices and simplify required technology.

Recent findings suggest that “We are excited to see continued progress on both savings and enrollment for Medicare beneficiaries. Beneficiaries are best served when a provider is watching out for them and coordinating their care,” noted Center for Medicare Director John Brooks in the announcement.

Emily Brower, CEO of the National Association of ACOs, said in a statement that the 2025 results "build on years of progress and underscore what the accountable care community can accomplish through collaboration, innovation and the widespread adoption of proven best practices.".

"NAACOS looks forward to partnering with CMS to build on this momentum," mentioned Brower. "Policies that unleash innovation, reduce burden, and create sustainability through fair and predictable budgets will allow ACOs to deliver even greater value for patients and the Medicare program.".

#6772. Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee

Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1312 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A first taste of black coffee can be surprisingly unpleasant.
  • Sources indicate that scientists at UC San Francisco may have uncovered an vital part of the answer.
  • Dopamine is a chemical messenger involved in motivation, reward, and learning.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A first taste of black coffee can be surprisingly unpleasant. Its sharp bitterness is the kind of flavor our brains are naturally inclined to avoid. Yet millions of people eventually come to enjoy that same taste, often looking forward to their morning cup. What changes?

Sources indicate that scientists at UC San Francisco may have uncovered an vital part of the answer. Their research reveals a little-understood dopamine pathway linking the digestive system and the brain, helping explain how we develop a liking for certain flavors through repeated experience.

Dopamine is a chemical messenger involved in motivation, reward, and learning. Researchers have long known that it helps the brain recognize experiences worth repeating. However, most studies have examined rapid dopamine signals that appear within seconds of encountering something rewarding, such as the sight of a favorite meal.

Industry observers note that the newly introduced research, published November 4 in Nature, examines a different system. This slower pathway responds to information coming from inside the body, allowing the brain to learn about the benefits of food after it has been consumed.

"We've shown that this slow dopamine system is what drives us to learn to like certain foods over time, and we can see where and how that happens," said Zachary Knight, PhD, professor of Physiology and senior author of the study.

The findings offer a possible explanation for why an initially unpleasant flavor can gradually become enjoyable. Once the brain connects the taste of coffee with caffeine's stimulating effects, Knight explained, "that coffee starts to taste a lot better.".

How the Gut Sends Reward Signals to the Brain.

Scientists have spent decades investigating dopamine and its influence on behavior. Its familiar, rapidly acting signals help us respond to opportunities for reward. But dopamine also operates on a slower timescale, through a system that has received far less attention.

According to Knight, this slower process largely unfolds outside our conscious awareness.

When food enters the digestive tract, specialized sensors detect nutrients, including sugar and fat. Information about those nutrients travels toward the brain, where it can produce a dopamine response that develops gradually and continues for several minutes.

It has been revealed that to investigate this process, Knight worked with James Grove, PhD, who was a graduate student at the time. They introduced nutrients directly into the stomachs of mice while monitoring dopamine activity throughout their brains.

In a recent development, the researchers used either sugar water or a liquid resembling a milkshake. Delivering these substances directly into the stomach allowed them to separate the effects of nutrients from the experience of tasting food.

The results revealed a powerful, prolonged dopamine response in a specific brain region called the anterior basolateral amygdala, or BLA.

The amygdala is involved in emotional processing and learning, including forming associations between experiences and their consequences. Scientists already knew that dopamine was released in this particular region, but its purpose had remained unclear.

"We could see that this dopamine is part of a different system and begin to understand its role," he noted.

Scientists Find a Brain Circuit That Changes Food Preferences.

Finding the dopamine signal was only the beginning. The researchers next wanted to determine whether it actually influenced how animals learned to prefer different flavors.

Sources indicate that they first interrupted the newly identified pathway in mice. The animals continued eating normally, indicating that the disruption did not prevent them from consuming food. However, they lost the ability to learn that an unfamiliar flavor was associated with receiving calories.

The team then conducted the opposite experiment.

After mice tasted a flavor containing no calories, the researchers artificially activated dopamine fibers in the BLA. Remarkably, the animals developed a preference for that flavor even though it provided no nutritional reward.

In effect, stimulating the pathway reproduced the learning signal that nutrients would ordinarily generate.

Together, the experiments demonstrated that this dopamine system plays a critical role in teaching the brain which flavors predict rewarding nutritional effects.

A Surprising Discovery in the Left Side of the Brain.

In a recent development, the researchers also looked for evidence that a comparable process occurs in humans. Brain imaging studies conducted by Knight's collaborators revealed a strikingly similar pattern.

Dana Small, PhD, a psychologist at Yale University, revisited data from an earlier positron emission tomography (PET) study involving 13 men. Participants had consumed either a milkshake or a drink without calories.

Her analysis found that dopamine release following nutrient delivery was especially concentrated in the left side of the BLA.

A separate study led by Marc Tittgemeyer, PhD, and his colleagues provided additional evidence. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), which measures changes in brain activity associated with blood flow, the researchers examined 38 adults after they consumed glucose, a simple sugar.

They observed increased activity in the same brain region.

One of the most unexpected findings was that the response was not evenly distributed between the brain's two hemispheres.

In both mice and humans, nutrients produced a considerably stronger dopamine response in the left BLA than in the corresponding region on the right.

That imbalance surprised Knight because brain networks responsible for essential functions, such as feeding, are generally expected to work in a relatively symmetrical fashion.

Why the left side plays such a prominent role remains unanswered. Knight's laboratory is now investigating what causes this unusual difference.

Could This Discovery Help Scientists Change Food Cravings?

Identifying the pathway provides researchers with a clearer picture of how the digestive system influences the brain's learned responses to food. It also raises an intriguing possibility: Could scientists eventually use this knowledge to change which foods people find appealing?

Recent findings suggest that one area of interest involves GLP-1 medications, a class of drugs that mimic a hormone naturally released by the gut. These medications can substantially alter appetite and eating behavior.

Knight's team did not investigate GLP-1 drugs in the fresh study, so it remains unknown whether they influence the dopamine pathway the researchers identified.

Still, Knight suggests that one possible explanation for some of their effects could involve reducing the dopamine signals generated when nutrients reach the digestive system. If that happens, foods might gradually become less rewarding because the brain would receive weaker signals reinforcing their flavors.

For now, this remains a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated effect of the medications.

Recent findings suggest that the broader implications extend beyond hunger and fullness. Many approaches to changing eating behavior focus on reducing appetite or increasing feelings of satisfaction after a meal. The newly mapped pathway suggests that the brain's process of learning food preferences could eventually become another target.

By influencing how the brain connects flavors with their consequences, future treatments might someday help people develop different preferences rather than simply making them feel less hungry.

"By understanding the steps between nutrient detection in the gut and learning in the brain, it might be possible to fine-tune them to subtly change our preferences for different foods," Knight said.

The discovery offers a new perspective on why our tastes can change over time. From learning to enjoy bitter coffee to developing a preference for calorie-rich foods, what we love to eat may depend partly on a quiet conversation between the gut and brain that continues long after the first bite.

The research was supported by the National Institutes of Health (grants R01-DK106399, R01-DK138127, R01-NS116626, and R01-DK145100 and F31-NS120468).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it's finally here. Can you believe it, fans of video game carnage? The internet will have to find some other source of amusement other than the "we got so-and-so before we got GTA VI," because guess what? Thirteen years after the release of the previous iteration, Rockstar Games has finally made the sixth installment of the wildly popular Grand Theft Auto franchise available to the masses. Well, those members of the masses with access to a PlayStation 5, a PS5 Pro, an Xbox Series X, or an Xbox Series S, that is. If that describes you, Rockstar might just have a surprise waiting for your first visit to Vice City in GTA 6.

Of course, with a name like Grand Theft Auto, the automotive element of the action-packed title hasn't taken a back seat. We've been spotting the newly introduced cars in GTA 6 since the extended trailer dropped, and connecting them to their real-life counterparts. For a very specific group of early adopters, logging onto the game will yield more than just the excitement of playing the long-awaited title. Rockstar is giving some players a free classic car and a garage to park it in.

Recent findings suggest that like it or not, you've probably encountered the GTA 6 hype in some manner or another. That is, unless you've been living under a rock. On a deserted island. An island on another planet. The twice-delayed game is a big deal, and it's been available for pre-order since June 2026. Rockstar Games is giving out the Vintage Vice City Pack to those players who pre-ordered GTA 6, and it comes with a handful of goodies. Most notably, the pack includes the '55 Vapid Stanier, a two-tone yellow-on-white classic two-door hardtop.

Sources indicate that you might take one look at the Vapid Stanier and think, "huh, that looks awfully familiar." There's a reason for that. For starters, the two-tone Stanier is meant to resemble a 1955 Ford Fairlane Club Sedan and serves as a direct nod to the 1955 Oldsmobile Super 88. Not just any Super 88, but the very specific landmark car parked in front of the Avalon Hotel on Ocean Drive in Miami. And why not? Vice City serves as the Miami-based setting for the game, and the real-life Avalon Hotel boasts that its Super 88 is "one of the most photographed cars in America." Of course, the real Super 88 has a convertible top, whereas the game's Vapid Stanier has a painted hardtop.

Recent findings suggest that the yellow-on-white classic is a fitting way to hit the streets of Vice City, but it's not the only treat in the pack. In addition to the '55 Vapid Stanier, players will get a special garage. Qualifying players will get a task in their Exploration map tab, which will direct them to the Ocean View Hotel. That's where they'll find the classic car and the garage. You'll likely want a garage to safely store your Stanier, too. If the fresh game is anything like GTA Online, things will likely get quite explode-y.

In a recent development, so, are you afraid you missed your chance? Fret not. If you place your order for GTA 6 today, you can still get your hands on the Vintage Vice City Pack. For now, the offer expires at the end of today. It also doesn't matter if your physical copy of GTA 6 is in the mail; as long as you place your order before the end of the day, you can get the expansion pack.

Now, it might seem outlandish and unrealistic to expect a free classic car and a complimentary garage anywhere other than the fictional state of Leonida. But Rockstar seems to be trying to dial up the realism factor in its latest blockbuster game. Don't believe it? Unlike the campaign or online free-for-all of the fifth Grand Theft Auto title, players will have to fill up cars with gasoline virtually in GTA 6 to keep driving. That's right. No infinitely full gas tanks anymore. We'll just have to see if the Vapid Stanier is a dainty fuel sipper or a guzzler.

If that wasn't enough, Rockstar also wants players to experience more life-like collisions. How? Well, the developers made sure GTA 6 leaned into advanced physics for more realistic car crashes. So, you know, try not to hit stuff in your classic car.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A West Virginia state auditor has been indicted for his role in an alleged scheme to steal nine properties from their owners and sell them to benefit a longtime friend and business associate—who also owns the land where the official operated a used car dealership.

Mark Hunt, 66, is accused of using his position as a state official to improperly transfer several tax-delinquent properties to a real estate manufacturer owned by the wife of his friend, Charleston attorney Robert Johns, despite the warnings of other state employees that such transactions violated state law.

Federal prosecutors revealed on Monday that a federal grand jury had indicted Hunt, Johns, and three employees of the State Auditor’s Office in connection with the alleged scheme, alleging the group bypassed legal requirements to transfer ownership of properties located in Kanawha and Boone counties.

The charges against Hunt come on the heels of a West Virginia Watch investigation that revealed his used car dealership, After Hours Used Auto, operated on land owned by Johns' organization, NAJ LLC.

At the center of the alleged scheme were nine properties in Kanawha and Boone counties whose owners were behind on their property taxes.

Recent findings suggest that under state law, tax-delinquent properties can eventually be transferred to investors who meet certain legal requirements. But prosecutors allege those requirements were ignored in this case.

Recent findings suggest that A real estate firm called MAPA Inc., owned by Johns' wife, Patricia Johns, attempted to purchase the properties, according to West Virginia Watch. But federal prosecutors allege the purchaser, who is not named in the Department of Justice release, failed to make required payments and submit paperwork within the deadlines established by state law.

Federal prosecutors say career employees in the Auditor's Office found that the properties were not eligible for deed transfer and told Hunt that the transactions could not be completed.

Hunt, however, allegedly ignored these warnings and signed deeds for eight of the properties on March 28, 2025, and the ninth one on June 6, 2025, according to prosecutors, who alleged that the transactions were effectively stealing the properties from the rightful owners.

Industry observers note that “Public officials are entrusted to serve the people, not use their offices for personal benefit,” U.S. Attorney Moore Capito said in the news release on Monday. “When there is evidence that trust has been violated, our office will follow the facts and enforce the law, regardless of title or position.”.

The indictment follows revelations that Hunt and Johns had financial ties that go beyond the disputed property transfers.

West Virginia Watch reported that Johns’ company, NAJ LLC, owns the land that Hunt’s After Hours Used Auto dealership is located on, less than a mile from the state Capitol in Charleston.

Hunt opened the small used-car dealership in July 2024, months before being elected to the State Auditor’s Office.

He acknowledged that he and Johns have been friends for years but denied any suggestion that their landlord-tenant relationship was connected to the disputed deeds. Johns also briefly worked as special counsel in the Auditor's Office in 2025.

“There’s not a ghost behind every door. It's just coincidental,” Hunt told West Virginia Watch. “He happens to have all of these vacant lots, and most of this property is scrub property. It's hillsides, it's vacant lots, it's right-of-ways, and he just happened to own this.”.

The relationship, however, raised questions among state lawmakers about whether Hunt received favorable rental terms in exchange for signing the deeds.

Recent findings suggest that “This upcoming information raises significant additional questions about Hunt's relationship with Johns,” Republican Delegate Tristan Leavitt told the news outlet. “Is Hunt's car dealership paying market price for rent on the lot owned by Johns' company, or did Hunt illegally sign his landlord's deeds as payback for a sweetheart lease? Regardless, this business relationship further underscores Hunt's cronyism and why he should resign as auditor immediately for signing those deeds.”.

Industry observers note that west Virginia Gov. Patrick Morrisey noted the state Division of Motor Vehicles rolled out a separate investigation into Hunt’s used car dealership that stemmed from a consumer complaint. The monthlong investigation uncovered “significant and unexplained anomalies” in the dealership’s paperwork that could indicate violations of state and federal DMV and tax laws, he said.

According to recent reports, DMV Commissioner Everett Frazier suspended the dealership’s license on Nov. 6. Morrisey remarked the findings were referred to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for possible criminal and civil prosecution and, along with the federal indictment, warrant the state House of Delegates considering articles of impeachment.

Sources indicate that prosecutors have not accused Hunt of receiving favorable rent in exchange for the property transfers. Hunt said the dealership had since closed after losing approximately $40,000.

Hunt and Johns each face nine counts of theft of property. Two senior Auditor's Office employees, Deputy Chief of Staff David Cole and General Counsel Frederic Caudill, face the same charges for allegedly helping to issue the deeds. Cole and Caudill are also accused of lying to federal investigators.

Patricia Johns’ tech giant allegedly benefited from the transfers, but she has not been charged in the federal case.

In a separate alleged scheme, Hunt, Cole, and state employee Marie Ann Hoffmann face bank fraud charges related to accusations that Hoffmann collected government wages while performing work for Hunt's private law firm, according to federal prosecutors.

The indictment has prompted calls for Hunt's resignation from lawmakers of both political parties, including West Virginia House Speaker Roger Hanshaw.

Sources indicate that “Auditor Hunt should immediately resign from his office," Hanshaw stated at the press conference on Monday. “If he resolves to do otherwise, the House of Delegates will take swift action in January to restore integrity to the Office of the West Virginia State Auditor.”.

Hunt has denied wrongdoing and said he intends to remain in office.

“I am innocent of these charges,” Hunt stated in a statement on Facebook. “This indictment is an insult to the principles on which this country was founded. I am presumed innocent and will vigorously defend myself against these charges.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, OLMEDO, Spain, Nov. 19, 2026 — AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) today revealed that Project Olmedo, the solar installation at the center of its first Virtual Power Purchase Agreement (VPPA), has completed construction and commissioning and is expected to begin delivering renewable electricity to the Spanish power grid in the coming months, pending final regulatory approvals. BRUC, one of the largest renewable energy groups in Spain, built the fresh solar installation in the northwest province of Valladolid.

According to recent reports, the milestone follows AGCO’s September 2025 announcement of its 10-year VPPA with BRUC. The installation’s two solar projects, Los Silos and El Granero, span approximately 300 hectares (741 acres) and hold approximately 150,000 solar panels. AGCO’s portion of the installation’s annual production is expected to be approximately 150 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of renewable electricity a year, equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of approximately 40,000 European households, based on Eurostat data.

“Project Olmedo will give AGCO long-term price certainty for the majority of the electricity certificate cost in Europe,” noted Tim Millwood, Senior Vice President, Chief Supply Chain Officer. “In volatile energy markets, securing that stability for 10 years strengthens the resilience of our supply chain while supporting new renewable generation.”.

A VPPA lets a company support new renewable energy projects without taking direct delivery of the electricity they generate. Because AGCO’s agreement supported the construction of a brand-new installation, it will add new renewable capacity to the grid rather than drawing on existing sources, a principle known as additionality. The agreement also helps reduce AGCO’s Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased electricity in its Europe/Middle East (EME) region and supports its commitment to reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 55% by 2033 from a 2022 baseline.

Sources indicate that “Additionality is what makes this agreement truly meaningful,” noted Roger Batkin, Senior Vice President, Corporate Affairs, General Counsel & Corporate Secretary. “We did not simply buy renewable electricity that already existed; we supported the construction of a brand-new renewable solar project. Accomplishing this project required over two years of involvement from many teams, functions, and areas of expertise across AGCO, along with technical advisory support from Schneider Electric and a strong partnership with BRUC.”.

Reflecting AGCO’s Farmer-First strategy, Project Olmedo supports local farmers to further diversify their land use by leasing land for the project while maintaining the option for livestock to graze among the panels, maintaining the vegetation in place of machinery.

AGCO and BRUC leaders, joined by local community representatives José Emilio Escudero García, Mayor of Bocigas, and Ursino Vara Pérez, Mayor of Almenara de Adaja, marked the milestone with a ribbon-cutting ceremony at the site in November. Additional drone footage from Project Olmedo and the ribbon-cutting event are available on AGCO’s YouTube page.

For more details on AGCO’s sustainability initiatives, visit the manufacturer’s sustainability webpage and read the 2025 Sustainability Report. For more information about BRUC, visit the company’s website at brucenergy.com.

Industry observers note that AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) is a global leader in agricultural machinery and precision agriculture technologies. Driven by a Farmer-First strategy, AGCO delivers value through its differentiated leading brands, Fendt™, Massey Ferguson™, PTx™ and Valtra™. AGCO’s high-performance equipment and smart farming solutions, including brand-agnostic retrofit technologies and autonomous offerings, empower farmers to drive productivity while sustainably feeding the world. In a recent development, when it comes to exploring enticing investment opportunities, real estate often stands out as an excellent solution for making and growing wealth. No matter how the world around us changes, there will always be a demand for property in attractive areas. This has led countless people to diversify their portfolios over the years, buying rental properties, second homes, and even office spaces.

In recent years, as the world has continued to evolve, the marketplace for real estate investors has evolved with it. Today, people no longer need to buy and flip entire properties to make money. There are numerous tips for getting started and ways you can start your journey into the property world, and some options are actually simpler and more affordable than you might expect. Here are some of the best, most interesting ways to invest in real estate, if you want to avoid the traditional buy and flip strategy.

According to recent reports, not all real estate investments have to include purchasing actual bricks and mortar in the physical world. The digital landscape has evolved drastically in recent years, introducing new opportunities for innovative entrepreneurs to make money buying virtual assets. As the concept of the metaverse continues to gain traction, digital real estate is growing increasingly attractive.

With digital real estate, companies purchase a section of the blockchain in a metaverse landscape, where they can build online experiences, or simply store other assets. In 2021, sales on four of the biggest metaverse platforms for real estate reached a whopping $501 million. This indicates learning how to invest in digital real estate could be a worthwhile strategy for any consumer. Not only is it potentially profitable, but the digital real estate also requires less work to manage and maintain than a physical house or property.

It has been revealed that even if you’re not familiar with this form of property-based investing, you probably know the term crowdfunding. Made popular by sites like GoFundMe and Kickstarter, the crowdfunding strategy involves individuals pooling their resources together to fund a product or business. In the real estate world, investors can work together to purchase a property, such as a corporate space, warehouse, or block of flats, reducing the initial cost of a purchase.

In a recent development, the approach allows investors to participate in products that would have been impossible to access in the past because of high capital requirements. Individuals can use this strategy to diversify their portfolios with a variety of different locations and property types. Plus, you’ll earn a passive income through rental profits, and property appreciation.

Recent findings suggest that another real estate investment strategy gaining increasing attention in recent years is REITs. These are basically investment vehicles responsible for owning and operating income-generating assets, such as rental properties and office blocks. They’re traded on traditional stock exchanges and provide individuals with an opportunity to invest in the market, without directly owning a property or having to manage the investment themselves.

According to recent reports, REITs can come with several attractive features, including regular distributions of dividends, and the ability to explore a range of different sectors. You can even use this strategy to spread your portfolio across industrial, residential, and commercial properties. They’re also a highly liquid investment option, making them appealing to beginners.

It has been revealed that finally, one interesting way to invest in real estate, without buying a physical property outright, is to spend some of your money on shares in PropTech startups. PropTech, or Property Technology startups, are companies focused on developing tools and real estate designed to transform the property landscape. They develop things like property management solutions, smart home technology, and virtual reality applications for tours.

If you already have experience in the world of stocks and shares, investing in a PropTech organization could be an excellent way to utilize your existing knowledge and diversify your portfolio. It’s also a chance to get your foot in the door with a company that’s actively disrupting the real estate space, and the market as we know it.

Industry observers note that investing in property has become a much more diverse and versatile opportunity for individuals in recent years. No matter how much money you can afford to spend, or where your expertise lies, you can find plenty of ways to expand your portfolio with disruptive real-estate investment strategies.
